1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <span>
18	#include <stdexcept>
19	#include <string>
20	
21	namespace hybrid {
22	
23	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
24	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
25	
26	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
27	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
28	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
29	
30	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
31	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
32	
33	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
34	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
35	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
36	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
37	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
38	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
39	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
40	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
41	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
42	
43	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
44	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
45	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
46	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
47	{
48	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
49	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
50	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
51	         | (0b111u << 12)
52	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
53	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
54	}
55	
56	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
57	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
58	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
59	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
60	{
61	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
62	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
63	         | (0b001u << 12)
64	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
65	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
66	}
67	
68	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
69	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
70	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
71	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
72	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
73	{
74	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
75	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
76	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
77	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
78	}
79	
80	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
81	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
82	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
83	//
84	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
85	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
86	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
87	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
88	// surfacing the fault.
89	template<typename Bus>
90	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
91	{
92	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
93	        throw std::runtime_error(
94	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
95	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
96	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
97	
98	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
99	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
100	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
101	
102	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
103	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
104	
105	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
106	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
107	
108	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
109	    if (cmderr != 0u)
110	        throw std::runtime_error(
111	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
112	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
113	}
114	
115	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
116	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
117	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
118	template<typename Bus>
119	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
120	{
121	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
122	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
123	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
124	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
125	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
126	                     "write_register_abstract");
127	}
128	
129	}  // namespace hybrid
